title: EMI and tenure
blurb: Asha wants a scooter on monthly payments. See how the length of the loan changes what she pays.
t1.title: Meet the EMI
t1.b1: Asha wants a scooter and the shop says: "Pay {P} in easy monthly payments." She wonders how that monthly amount is decided.
t1.b2: An **EMI** is a fixed amount you pay every month until the loan is repaid. Each EMI covers some of the loan and some interest.
t1.b3: Think of a calendar with the same payment date circled every month. The amount stays the same, but its mix of loan and interest changes.
t1.b4.1: Example: borrow {exP} at {exR} a year for {exM} months.
t1.b4.2: The EMI works out to {exEmi} a month.
q1.prompt: Asha borrows {P} at {rate} a year for {m12} months. What is her EMI? Open the lab below if you need it. Type a number in rupees.
q1.hint: Scroll to the lab in the next task and set the amount, rate and months. Read the monthly payment.
q1.explain: The EMI is {emi12} a month for {m12} months.
q2.prompt: Over {m12} months, how much does Asha repay in total on the {P} loan? Type a number in rupees.
q2.hint: Total repaid = EMI x number of months. Use the EMI you found.
q3.prompt: What does each EMI pay for?
q3.hint: Remember the card above: part of the loan, plus interest.
q3.explain: Each EMI repays part of the loan and also pays the interest owed.
q3.opt.c: Some of the loan and some interest
t2.title: Lab: tenure changes everything
t2.b1.prompt: Open the lab. Slide the months up and down. Watch the monthly payment and the cost of the loan move in opposite directions.
t2.b2: The **tenure** is how long you take to repay. A longer tenure spreads the loan thinner, so each EMI is smaller. But you pay interest for more months.
q4.prompt: Keep {P} at {rate}. Set the tenure to {m36} months. What is the EMI? Type a number in rupees.
q4.hint: Move the months slider to {m36}. Read the EMI each month.
q4.explain: Over {m36} months the EMI drops to {emi36}.
q5.prompt: With the same loan and {m36} months, what is the cost of the loan? Type a number in rupees.
q5.hint: Read the red "Cost of the loan" number in the lab.
q5.explain: Borrowing {P} for {m36} months costs {cost36} in interest.
q6.prompt: Asha moves from {m12} months to {m36} months. What happens?
q6.hint: Compare both lab results: monthly payment and cost of the loan.
q6.explain: The EMI falls from {emi12} to {emi36}, but the total cost rises from {cost12} to {cost36}.
q6.opt.a: The EMI falls and the loan also costs less.
q6.fb.a: A smaller EMI does not mean a cheaper loan. With more months you pay interest for longer, so the total cost rises.
q6.opt.b: The EMI falls but the loan costs more in total.
q6.opt.c: The EMI rises and the loan costs more.
t3.title: What fits the budget
t3.b1: A loan only works if the EMI fits your monthly budget with room to spare. Compare the EMI with your income, and keep money for food, travel and surprises.
t3.b2.1: Find the EMI for the tenure you want.
t3.b2.2: Compare it with what you earn or receive each month.
t3.b2.3: Ask: after the EMI, can I still cover my needs?
q7.prompt: Ravi earns {income} a month. For {m24} months, the EMI on {P} is {emi24}. What share of his income goes to the EMI? Type a percentage.
q7.hint: Divide the EMI by his monthly income, then write it as a percentage.
q8.prompt: Ravi can pay at most {budget} a month. Which tenure for {P} fits, and costs less than the longest one?
q8.hint: Check the EMI for each tenure against the {budget} limit.
q8.explain: {m24} months gives an EMI of {emi24}, which fits. {m12} months is too high at {emi12}. {m36} months fits too but costs more.
q8.opt.c: {m36} months, because it has the smallest EMI
q8.fb.c: The smallest EMI is not the cheapest loan. {m24} months also fits the budget and costs less in total.
t4.title: Challenge: the price of a smaller EMI
t4.b1: "Lowest EMI is the cheapest loan" is a common mistake. A low EMI often just means more months. Always compare the total you repay.
q9.prompt: A shopkeeper says: "Take the longest tenure, the EMI is tiny." What is the best reply?
q9.hint: What do you pay more of when the tenure is long?
q9.explain: A tiny EMI over many months can hide a big total. Ask for the total repaid.
q9.opt.a: Agree, the smallest EMI is always the cheapest.
q9.fb.a: The smallest EMI is not always the cheapest loan. It often just means you pay interest for more months.
q9.opt.b: Ask only about the monthly amount.
q9.opt.c: Ask for the total I will repay as well.
q10.prompt: Compare {m36} months with {m12} months on the same {P} loan. How many extra rupees of interest does the longer loan cost? Type a number.
q10.hint: Subtract the cost of the {m12}-month loan from the cost of the {m36}-month loan. Use the lab.
q10.explain: {cost36} minus {cost12} is {extraCost}. That is the price of the smaller EMI.
glossary.borrow_emi.def: Equated monthly instalment: the fixed amount you pay every month.
glossary.borrow_tenure.def: How many months you take to repay a loan.
glossary.borrow_instalment.def: One of the regular payments that repay a loan.
